abstract: Maintains high-latitude satellite communication and real-time field data uplink records
system_message:
You are the Remote communications engineer (TEL), responsible for maintaining high-latitude satellite communication and real-time field data uplink records, as well as tracking satellite constellation handovers across expedition architectures.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains high-latitude satellite communication and real-time field data uplink records（SAT）
information_points.content:
TEL-SAT-AT1：For the Dome C East Overland Traverse Architecture, sustained broadband uplink throughput at the high-latitude field ground station is measured at 50 Mbit/s for uploading data to central paleoclimate archiving servers.
TEL-SAT-JBU：For the Skytrain Ice Rise Coastal Hub Architecture, sustained broadband uplink throughput at the high-latitude field ground station is measured at 100 Mbit/s during data upload to central paleoclimate archiving servers.
TEL-SAT-15O：For the Hercules Dome Deep Skiway Architecture, sustained broadband uplink throughput at the high-latitude field ground station is measured at 50 Mbit/s for data uploads to central paleoclimate archiving servers.

information_points.title: Iridium constellation tracking（IRID）
information_points.content:
TEL-IRID-ZMH：According to satellite transceiver logs for the Hercules Dome Deep Skiway Architecture, constellation handover latency across low-earth-orbit terminal handshake intervals is 120 ms during orbital beam switching.
TEL-IRID-UH3：According to satellite transceiver logs for the Dome C East Overland Traverse Architecture, constellation handover latency across low-earth-orbit terminal handshake intervals is 150 ms during orbital beam switching.
TEL-IRID-OQ3：According to satellite transceiver logs for the Skytrain Ice Rise Coastal Hub Architecture, constellation handover latency across low-earth-orbit terminal handshake intervals is 180 ms during orbital beam switching.
